identity.title: LongWriter-Zero: Mastering Ultra-Long Text Generation via Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: LLMs struggle to generate ultra-long text because of maximum-length limits and quality degradation with increasing sequence length.

gap.claim: Synthetic-data-based supervised fine-tuning is costly to construct and may produce incoherent, inconsistent, artificial, and structurally monotonous outputs.

contributions.claim: An incentivization-based RL approach trains from a base model without annotated or synthetic data to develop ultra-long generation capabilities.
The approach uses reasoning for planning and refinement, supported by reward models targeting length control, writing quality, and structural formatting.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by developing ultra-long generation through RL from scratch without annotated or synthetic data.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LongWriter-Zero, trained from Qwen2.5-32B, consistently outperforms traditional SFT methods on long-form writing tasks.
The authors report state-of-the-art results across all metrics on WritingBench and Arena-Write.
The authors report surpassing DeepSeek R1 and Qwen3-235B, described as 100B+ models, on these evaluations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Ultra-long generation is demanded but constrained by length limits and worsening quality.
Prior LongWriter-style methods use synthetic long-form outputs for supervised fine-tuning, with substantial data-construction and quality drawbacks.
LongWriter-Zero replaces this dependence with RL from a base model, encouraging planning and refinement during writing.
The authors report broad benchmark gains over SFT methods and larger named models.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links distinct writing objectives—length control, quality, and formatting—to specialized reward models, then reports results across named benchmarks and metrics.

lessons.interpretation: Separating controllable objectives can make the training rationale and evidence alignment more inspectable.
lessons.application: For a multi-objective generation method, define each reward target explicitly and report results broken down by corresponding evaluation dimensions.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when objectives are inseparable or when reliable objective-specific evaluators are unavailable.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the benchmark metric values, training procedure, reward-model construction, or statistical uncertainty.
The comparative setup and model-size details beyond the named models are not specified.
